verdicts.why: In the S5 finale May goes to Tahiti with the retiring Coulson while the Zephyr leaves 'with their friends continuing their S.H.I.E.L.D. missions without them'. The wiki says that after he died she 'returned to S.H.I.E.L.D.' as Mack's second (S6).
Wiki 'Retirement' section: once the Chronicom Colonization was over, 'Fitz and Jemma Simmons decided to retire from S.H.I.E.L.D.' (S7 finale). The infobox lists S.H.I.E.L.D. as former.
This is the same Fitz as A:st-leo-fitz, who retires from S.H.I.E.L.D. with Simmons after the S7 finale. The twin's last S.H.I.E.L.D. stage needs the same S7 departure.
Wiki: Simmons and Fitz 'decided to retire from S.H.I.E.L.D.' after the Chronicom war. In the one-year-later reunion Mack won't share classified details 'as she was no longer an agent'.

In S2E20 'Scars' Mack tells Coulson he is leaving S.H.I.E.L.D., turns down reassignment and hands over his badge. In 'S.O.S. Part Two' (the S2 finale) 'Mackenzie was convinced to rejoin S.H.I.E.L.D.' by Coulson.

In S3E17 'The Team', after the Hive lockdown, she demands to walk away and leaves the Playground 'away from the Secret Warriors'. Later in S3 she 'was eventually convinced to return to S.H.I.E.L.D.' (Emancipation). The Slingshot stage only repeated a group she was already in, and her solo revenge trip there is acting alone, not a move.
Hunter was an SAS lieutenant (Basra 2008, Sierra Leone 2011) 'before becoming a mercenary for hire'. He is already a mercenary when S2 begins, so the British Army is backstory.

In the S2 finale Lincoln turns against Jiaying and Afterlife falls. At the start of S3 he 'decided to shun his past life and wanted nothing to do with the Inhumans', works at Cincinnati Memorial Hospital, and joins S.H.I.E.L.D. only later in S3.

No True Believers membership is shown: he is brought to their Zephyr, Voss locks him in a cage, and he sides with S.H.I.E.L.D. (the wiki heading means believing the prophecy). Deke Shaw's Company is his own workplace, which the record doesn't track and the dataset doesn't name, so the single S6 S.H.I.E.L.D. stage (Mack makes him an agent) stands.

In S3E17 Joey says he wants to leave S.H.I.E.L.D. as soon as possible. Once cleared he 'was allowed to return home, turning his back on the Secret Warriors for good and returning to his former life'. The infobox lists both S.H.I.E.L.D. and the Secret Warriors as former.

In 'The Bridge' (S1E10) Mike is a S.H.I.E.L.D. trainee who joins the team on the Bus before Centipede takes him. At Cybertek (S1 finale) he kills Garrett, declines Skye's offer to join Coulson's team and leaves on his own. In S2 he 'accepted Coulson's invitation to join the newly rebuilt S.H.I.E.L.D.'

Asgard is backstory: he stayed behind on Earth centuries ago when the Berserker host went home, and he has no tie to Asgard in ep 8 or ep 46. Seville is then his only group from his first title, so it takes the record's '(from the start)' form.

In ep 8 he only wonders whether 'it's time to start over somewhere else' and Coulson suggests Portland. No departure from the university is shown, and the wiki infobox still lists the University of Seville as current. A night in a Norway jail cell (ep 46) doesn't show he left, so this unsure case keeps what's there.

'S.H.I.E.L.D. from the start' is wrong: he is a Chronicom observer who abducts the team (S4E22), and Hunters decommission him in S6E3. The proposal leaves out a rejoin: in S6E5 he betrays Daisy's team and 'joined [Atarah] and the others', then in S6E6 he chooses his friends and shuts Atarah down. He sides with S.H.I.E.L.D. from S6E13 (his Hunter role is undercover).

The S.H.I.E.L.D. claim rests on the recreated Flint enrolling at Coulson Academy, a school the record doesn't track as a group (the owner is deciding those separately). Guarding the module with Piper in the S7 finale is a favor, not a join.

He served in the Army's 28th Infantry in WWII and had to leave the battlefield after losing his leg at Bastogne. He is already an SSR agent when Agent Carter S1 opens in 1946, so the Army is backstory.

Jarvis was dishonorably discharged from the British Army during WWII, when Howard Stark saved him from a court martial. In Agent Carter he is only Stark's man, so the Army is backstory and Stark Industries is his single group.
Thompson was a WWII Navy lieutenant who 'joined the Strategic Scientific Reserve following the end of the war'. He is SSR throughout Agent Carter, so the Navy is backstory.
Dooley was an Army officer in WWII and 'returned home' when the war ended. In Agent Carter S1 he is chief of the New York SSR only, so the Army is backstory.
Wilkes was a Navy engineer during WWII and is already an Isodyne scientist in Agent Carter S2, so the Navy is backstory.

At the end of S1E9 the Watcher sends the Guardians home. T'Challa goes back to his universe and is teaching Peter Quill to use a blaster as a Ravager. The infobox lists the Ravagers as current and the Guardians of the Multiverse as former.
At the end of S1E9 the Guardians go home through the pub door and Thor rejoins Jane in his own universe. The infobox lists his Asgard as current and the Guardians as former.

The proposal is right: in S2E4 she is Thanos' daughter and assassin, then turns on him and kills him. She joins the Guardians in S1E9 and goes home to Tony when the team breaks up (infobox: Guardians formerly, no current group). The placeholder 'Thanos' forces' becomes 'The Children of Thanos', the name the dataset already uses for Nebula.

At the end of S1E9 the Guardians disband and the Watcher sends Natasha to the universe that lost its Widow. There Fury offers her a place in the new Avengers against the Asgardian invasion. The infobox lists that universe's Avengers as current and the Guardians as former.
